To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of studies of youth psychosomatic treatments has increased over time but the number of unique treatment elements identified has not.

(1) the number of new treatment protocols has not kept up with the number of new studies; (2) new studies have not led to new practice elements for all problem areas; (3) the most common problem areas are anxiety, disruptive behavior, and attention/hyperactivity; (4) the least common problem areas are eating disorders, mania, suicide, and substance use; and (5) the most common practice elements are psychoeducation and parent involvement.
